newsitem.title: UK: BT, MCI plan global ATM services.
newsitem.headline: BT, MCI plan global ATM services.

text.p: British Telecommunications Plc said on Thursday that its joint venture with MCI, called Concert, planned to offer a global service that sends voice and data into a single, high-speed network.
"This will enable the alliance to improve considerably economies of scale through the use of a common broadband infrastructure," BT said in a statement.
ATM technology, or asynchronous transfer mode, is already used by Concert in 13 countries including the UK, U.S., the Netherlands, France, Germany, Sweden, Australia and Japan.
BT and MCI plan to extend their national ATM services to offer bilateral trans-Atlantic commercial ATM services in early 1997. Later in 1997, the service would be expanded to more countries, BT said.
The last phase would be for Concert to offer end-to-end ATM services with multiple options for access methods, based on versatile end-user equipment and service gateways.
"This will enable customers to establish seamless services with higher functionality and service levels," the group stated.

Stephen Von Rump, MCI's vice president of enterprise marketing, said the global market for ATM, which makes it possible to simultaneously transmit voice, data, fax and video over a single network, was expected to grow by 300 percent in the next several years.
